- **bonsaiPhaseToast.ts** (src/utils/bonsaiPhaseToast.ts) — *Phase toast manager*: Show and replace single-stack Decky toasts for in-flight Ask phase updates.
- **bonsaiReplyReadyToast.ts** (src/utils/bonsaiReplyReadyToast.ts) — *Ask reply ready toast*: Show one terminal toast per completed/failed background Ask when reply surface is hidden.
- **bonsaiReplySurface.ts** (src/utils/bonsaiReplySurface.ts) — *Reply surface visibility state*: Track whether Main tab reply surface is visible and queue QAM open from toast taps.
- **bonsaiSessionSurvival.ts** (src/utils/bonsaiSessionSurvival.ts) — *Session survival snapshot*: Capture and restore Main-tab Ask state across Decky Content remounts (modals, tab switches).
- **buildAnswerBubbleElement.tsx** (src/utils/buildAnswerBubbleElement.tsx) — *The reply bubble*: Builds the bubble holding one answer from the AI — either one still arriving word by word, or a finished one read back from history. An answer is not drawn as a single block of text. It is cut into sections, and each section is a place the D-pad can stop, so a person can walk down a long answer instead of jumping past it. This file decides where those stops are, and what happens when someone presses past the top or bottom edge of the bubble.
- **buildReplyActionsElement.tsx** (src/utils/buildReplyActionsElement.tsx) — *Reply actions row builder*: Builds everything that can sit under one AI reply, below the answer itself: the Helpful / Not really thumbs, the "what went wrong" chips that appear once someone picks Not really, an optional Read aloud line, and the Show details line. Not every reply shows all of them — one still arriving, or one already rated, shows fewer.
- **buildThinkingBlurbTextElement.tsx** (src/utils/buildThinkingBlurbTextElement.tsx) — *Thinking blurb text element builder*: Render thinking status copy with italic prose, upright glyphs, spoilers redacted.
- **buildTurnHeaderElement.tsx** (src/utils/buildTurnHeaderElement.tsx) — *Turn header element builder*: Build the question bubble for a turn — its text, and the Retry icon in its corner.
- **chatPanelScroll.ts** (src/utils/chatPanelScroll.ts) — *Chat panel scroll helpers*: Locate QAM TabContentsScroll, scroll panels by step, and geometry nudges for clipped content.
- **chatSlotTurns.ts** (src/utils/chatSlotTurns.ts) — *Chat slot turn mapper*: Convert persisted slot turns into collapsed Ask transcript pairs.
- **chatSlotsApi.ts** (src/utils/chatSlotsApi.ts) — *Chat slots RPC client*: Thin wrappers for chat slot list/get/create/delete/rename RPCs.
- **chatTurnTitle.ts** (src/utils/chatTurnTitle.ts) — *Collapsed/expanded turn title builder*: Build user question labels for Ask thread turn headers — a one-line truncated title for a closed turn, and the whole question (whitespace-normalized, un-truncated) for an open one.
- **clearBonsaiBrowserStorage.ts** (src/utils/clearBonsaiBrowserStorage.ts) — *bonsAI browser storage clearer*: Remove every bonsai* key from localStorage and sessionStorage (both the `bonsai:` and `bonsai_` spellings).
- **clipboardStash.ts** (src/utils/clipboardStash.ts) — *Clipboard stash sanitizer*: Read host clipboard via RPC and sanitize text before attaching to Ask input.
- **clipboardWrite.ts** (src/utils/clipboardWrite.ts) — *Clipboard write*: Copy text to the host clipboard from the reply Copy action.
- **contextChipsFromSnapshot.ts** (src/utils/contextChipsFromSnapshot.ts) — *Context chips from snapshot*: Derive sorted context chips and transparency UI availability from input transparency snapshots.
- **createTabLocalSurvival.ts** (src/utils/createTabLocalSurvival.ts) — *Tab local survival factory*: Factory for tab-local UI snapshots that survive Decky modal unmount/remount cycles.
- **deckSliderMath.ts** (src/utils/deckSliderMath.ts) — *Deck slider math*: Clamp, index/percent mapping, and Deck button direction helpers for discrete sliders.
- **deckyCall.ts** (src/utils/deckyCall.ts) — *Decky RPC helpers*: Wrap Decky `call()` with deadlines and normalize error payloads for UI toasts.
- **desktopChatAutosave.ts** (src/utils/desktopChatAutosave.ts) — *Desktop chat autosave tracker*: Track which Ask request_ids were auto-saved to desktop chat notes in sessionStorage.
- **drgGlossaryAsk.ts** (src/utils/drgGlossaryAsk.ts) — *DRG glossary explain-further Ask composer*: Build the auto-sent Ask question and thread label for a glossary term's "explain further" chip.
- **drgGlossaryTermMatch.ts** (src/utils/drgGlossaryTermMatch.ts) — *DRG Survivor glossary term matching*: Find curated DRG Survivor jargon terms inside reply text so they can be marked up as tappable.
- **drgGlossaryTermRegistry.ts** (src/utils/drgGlossaryTermRegistry.ts) — *DRG glossary term chip registry*: Track mounted DRG glossary term chips so D-pad Down/Up can park the ring on one in passing.
- **focusNavigation.ts** (src/utils/focusNavigation.ts) — *Focus navigation key helpers*: Normalize Deck/keyboard D-pad and stick direction keys for onMove and key handlers.
- **i18n.ts** (src/utils/i18n.ts) — *UI string translator*: Resolve localized UI strings for the effective Ask reply language with English fallback.
- **inputTransparency.ts** (src/utils/inputTransparency.ts) — *Input transparency types*: Types and helpers for Show details context-chip ladder snapshots from RPC.
- **intentPackSearch.ts** (src/utils/intentPackSearch.ts) — *Intent pack search*: Build search index and match SETTINGS_DATABASE rows with offline intent pack aliases.
- **joinPresetWithRunningGame.ts** (src/utils/joinPresetWithRunningGame.ts) — *Preset text passthrough*: Preserves a single helper for preset chip inject into the Ask field.
- **liveTurnFocusGraph.ts** (src/utils/liveTurnFocusGraph.ts) — *Live turn focus graph*: D-pad focus helpers for the live Ask turn (answer bubble → strategy branches → checklist → reply actions).
- **localOnlyAskCommands.ts** (src/utils/localOnlyAskCommands.ts) — *Local-only Ask commands*: Detect sanitizer, shortcut-setup, and VAC-check keyword commands that skip Ollama.
- **mediaFormat.ts** (src/utils/mediaFormat.ts) — *Turning screenshot and file info into words a person can read*: When the screenshot browser shows a list of captured files, this file turns raw computer data into the words shown next to each one: the file's path becomes a link that can actually be opened as a picture, the moment it was taken becomes something like "8/14/2026, 3:02 PM" instead of a number of seconds since 1970, and the file's size becomes "2.4 MB" instead of a large number of bytes.
- **mergePullModelCatalog.ts** (src/utils/mergePullModelCatalog.ts) — *Combining the built-in model list with an update from the back end*: The Pull Models screen shows a list of AI models a person can download. That list ships with the plugin (the "bundled" list) so it works even with no internet, but the project also publishes updates to it — new models, models that got pulled, corrected details — and this file combines the two: it starts from the bundled list, then lays a downloaded update on top of it one model at a time, throwing out anything in the update that does not look like a real model entry.
- **modelRoutingOrder.ts** (src/utils/modelRoutingOrder.ts) — *Which installed AI model to try first*: A person can have more than one AI model installed at once. Ask can use any of them, but needs a starting order to try them in, and the Ollama tab needs to show that order as a list. This file holds the built-in starting order — one for a plain question, a separate one for a question that includes a picture — plus the rules for whether a model looks like it can handle pictures, whether a model is large enough that it is a bad idea to run on the Deck's shared graphics memory, and whether a model's licence is allowed under the current Settings licence tier. It builds the final "try these, in this order" list that both the Ollama tab's preview and the actual Ask request use.
- **navFocusRegistry.ts** (src/utils/navFocusRegistry.ts) — *Sending the controller's highlight to a different part of the screen*: The Steam Deck's controller does not click on things — it moves a highlight ("focus") from one control to the next, and Steam itself, not the plugin, decides which element that highlight sits on. Most of the screen is one connected area, so the highlight moves normally with the D-pad. A few places on the Main tab — the strip that shows what game is running, the row of chat slots, and the permission-hint rows shown under the transcript — sit in their own separate areas, and moving the highlight into one of those from the reply row needs a different trick than an ordinary D-pad move. This file is that trick: each of those areas registers itself here while it is on screen, and this file's `takeNavFocus()` is the one approved way to move the controller's highlight into one of them.
- **ollamaTabLocalSurvival.ts** (src/utils/ollamaTabLocalSurvival.ts) — *Remembering the Ollama tab across a panel close and reopen*: Opening certain modals tears down and rebuilds the quick-access panel, which would normally reset the Ollama tab to its starting state. This file remembers what that tab looked like right before the panel closes — the connection status, the list of hosts found on the local network, any discovery message, and whether the "install Ollama locally" menu was open — and hands it back so the tab looks the same when the panel reopens.
- **permissionDeepLink.ts** (src/utils/permissionDeepLink.ts) — *Knowing which Permissions row unblocks which action*: When something a person tries to do is blocked because a permission is off — for example, asking to check a Steam ban when "Steam ban lookup" is off — this file knows which row on the Permissions tab controls that permission, and the exact sentence to show explaining what to turn on.
- **permissionJumpRegistry.ts** (src/utils/permissionJumpRegistry.ts) — *Remembering a jump to the Permissions tab, and finishing it*: When a denied permission shows a "go fix this" link — for example from a chat message explaining that a permission is off — pressing it needs to remember two things across the tab switch that follows: which tab to come back to, and which row on the Permissions tab the controller's highlight should land on once it gets there. This file remembers both, and moves the highlight once the Permissions tab has actually rendered that row.
- **persistOllamaIp.ts** (src/utils/persistOllamaIp.ts) — *Remembering the network Ollama address, only when it is actually in use*: The plugin can talk to an AI model running on the Deck itself, or to one running on another PC on the same network. This file makes sure the remembered network address only gets overwritten while the Deck is actually set to talk to that other PC — never while it is set to run models on the Deck itself.
- **presetCarouselInject.ts** (src/utils/presetCarouselInject.ts) — *Turning a back-end "insert this chip" message into something the carousel can use*: The row of suggested-question chips above the Ask box (the "preset carousel") can be told by the back end to drop a specific chip of text into it — for example, after a background check finishes and has something worth suggesting. That message comes from the back end already loosely shaped, in a form TypeScript cannot fully trust; this file checks it actually contains real text before handing it to the carousel, and returns nothing usable (`null`) if it does not.
- **pullModelCatalogRefresh.ts** (src/utils/pullModelCatalogRefresh.ts) — *Pull model catalog refresh bus*: Pub/sub notify listeners to refresh the living pull-model catalog overlay.
- **pullModelRecommendations.ts** (src/utils/pullModelRecommendations.ts) — *Suggesting which model to download next*: The Pull Models screen can suggest a model to download based on what is missing from what is already installed. This file works out what is missing — a fast small model, a strategy-guide model, an "expert"-level model, or a model that can read pictures — and scores the catalog entries by roughly how good the answer is for how much the download costs in space, so the best fit for the gap gets suggested first.
- **redactThinkingBlurbSpoilers.ts** (src/utils/redactThinkingBlurbSpoilers.ts) — *Thinking blurb spoiler redaction*: Turn model-authored [[spoiler]]…[[/spoiler]] spans in the thinking line into blocks.
- **replyStopRegistry.ts** (src/utils/replyStopRegistry.ts) — *Moving the controller's highlight between a reply's small buttons*: An Ask or Strategy reply on the Main tab has several small controls around it — Retry, Copy, the Helpful / Not really buttons, Read aloud, and Show details — and a person using a controller needs to move the highlight between them with the D-pad. This file keeps a live map from each control's name to the actual on-screen element currently mounted for it, and can move the controller's highlight to any of them by name.
- **runningGameCharacterSuggestions.ts** (src/utils/runningGameCharacterSuggestions.ts) — *Suggesting an AI character based on the game you're playing*: When the AI-character feature is on and a person opens the character picker, this works out up to three characters from the built-in catalog that fit whatever game is currently running — so someone playing a game with catalog characters sees them offered first, instead of having to search a long list by hand.
- **sessionRagChipCandidates.ts** (src/utils/sessionRagChipCandidates.ts) — *Asking for chip suggestions drawn from this game's own notes*: Before showing the row of suggested-question chips for the game currently being played, the plugin can ask the back end for chip text drawn from that game's own notes (its entry in the plugin's knowledge base), rather than only the fixed set built into the plugin. This file makes that request and turns whatever comes back into a clean list of chips the carousel can use, dropping anything that arrives without real text or a category.
- **settingsPanelScroll.ts** (src/utils/settingsPanelScroll.ts) — *What "Up" should do at the top of a scrolled Settings section*: On the Settings and Ollama tabs, some sections are taller than the screen and scroll. When a person moving the controller's highlight upward reaches the top control in a scrolled section, pressing Up should not do nothing — it should first reveal more of the section above, and once there is nothing left to reveal, hand the highlight to the tab strip along the top. This file is that chain of fallbacks.
- **settingsPayload.ts** (src/utils/settingsPayload.ts) — *Turning the settings on screen into the message that saves them*: The Settings tab holds every setting under a screen-side name, spelled the way screen code spells things. The back end that writes them to disk knows the same settings under different names, spelled its own way. This file is the translation between the two, and it is the only place that translation is written down. Hand it everything the screen currently has and it hands back the one object the back end is expecting, with all fifty-odd settings renamed.
- **settingsTabLocalSurvival.ts** (src/utils/settingsTabLocalSurvival.ts) — *Remembering the Settings tab's open menu across a panel close and reopen*: Opening certain modals tears down and rebuilds the quick-access panel, which would normally reset the Settings tab. This file remembers one thing about it — whether the AI character's accent-intensity menu was left open — so it looks the same when the panel reopens instead of resetting closed.
- **splitResponseIntoChunks.ts** (src/utils/splitResponseIntoChunks.ts) — *Breaking a long reply into D-pad-sized pieces*: A finished Ask or Strategy reply can be long. Showing it as one solid block would mean a single D-pad press scrolls through all of it with no stopping point along the way, so this file breaks a reply up into a few pieces first, each becoming its own stop the D-pad can land on. It never cuts a piece of code in the middle — a fenced code block (a part of a reply wrapped in three backticks) always stays whole in one piece.
- **splitThinkingBlurbItalicSegments.ts** (src/utils/splitThinkingBlurbItalicSegments.ts) — *Thinking blurb italic segments*: Split thinking status copy so emoji graphemes stay upright while prose stays italic.
- **spoilerFenceRegistry.ts** (src/utils/spoilerFenceRegistry.ts) — *Letting the D-pad land on a hidden spoiler instead of scrolling past it*: Reply text can contain a "spoiler" that starts out hidden until a person chooses to reveal it. Normally the whole reply is one connected area for the controller's Down button to scroll through, so a hidden spoiler inside it never gets its own stop — Down just scrolls past it, and with no touchscreen there is no other way to reach it. This file keeps a live list of every hidden spoiler currently on screen, so Down can check that list and land the controller's highlight on one of them instead of scrolling past.
- **steamInputJump.ts** (src/utils/steamInputJump.ts) — *Jumping straight to Steam's own controller-setup screens*: A few Ask replies about controller setup can offer a direct jump to Steam's own Input configuration screens instead of only describing where to find them — for example "map a button" or "open the controller layout for this game". This file makes that jump happen: it tries Steam's own in-app screens first, and falls back to a `steam://` link if that fails or is not available for that particular target.
- **steamParental.ts** (src/utils/steamParental.ts) — *Watching Steam's own Kids lock*: Steam has its own "Kids" parental lock, and this file watches it for as long as the plugin is open, so the rest of the plugin can lock itself down to match — without ever writing the lock state to the plugin's own saved settings. It exists because Steam's own subscription for this can behave in a few different unhelpful ways depending on the Deck, and this file has to work correctly no matter which one happens.
- **strategyChecklist.ts** (src/utils/strategyChecklist.ts) — *Turning a model's checklist into something the screen can trust*: In Strategy mode, the model can hand back a checklist — a title and a list of steps — instead of only prose, and the person can tick items off as they go. This file turns whatever the back end sends for that checklist into a shape the screen can trust, keeps a person's ticked-off items when the model sends a revised list of steps on the next reply (matching by wording when the ids themselves changed), and builds the two request shapes that go back to the back end: one for continuing the conversation, one for saving progress.
- **strategyChecklistPersistence.ts** (src/utils/strategyChecklistPersistence.ts) — *Saving Strategy checklist progress without saving on every single tick*: Ticking a box on the Strategy checklist should feel instant, but saving every single tick to the back end the moment it happens would mean a flurry of save requests during a quick run through a list. This file waits briefly after the last change before actually saving, so a burst of ticks becomes one save, while still saving right away when the person leaves the checklist or clears it.
- **strategyGuideBranches.ts** (src/utils/strategyGuideBranches.ts) — *Turning a model's fork in the conversation into something the screen can trust*: A Strategy reply can offer the person a fork in the conversation — "want the early-game plan, or the boss fight?" — as a set of labelled choices instead of plain prose. This file turns whatever the back end sends for that fork into a shape the screen can trust, or nothing at all if the shape does not hold up.
- **streamMarkdownPrepare.ts** (src/utils/streamMarkdownPrepare.ts) — *Stream markdown preparer*: Progressive markdown layout for token streaming with closed-block safety and wait chips.
- **stripAssistantDisplayTags.ts** (src/utils/stripAssistantDisplayTags.ts) — *Catching any control tag the back end missed before it reaches the screen*: The model writes a couple of tags into its own reply that are only meant for the plugin to read — a status line wrapped in `<bonsai-status>`, and a strategy-branch marker — and those are supposed to be removed by the back end before the reply is ever shown. This file is the safety net for when that removal is missed, most often on a reply that continues across more than one turn: it strips both kinds of tag from whatever text is about to be displayed, including a tag that is still only half-written because the reply was cut off mid-stream.
- **stripSoftContinueCue.ts** (src/utils/stripSoftContinueCue.ts) — *Cleaning up a "Continuing…" note that was still showing when Stop was pressed*: While an Ask is still being answered, the screen shows a small "Continuing…" note at the end of the reply so far, to make clear more text is on the way. If a person presses Stop at almost exactly the moment that note is about to be cleared, the saved reply can end up keeping the note as if it were part of the actual answer. This file is a backstop that removes a trailing "Continuing…" from a reply that has already been stopped and saved.
- **tabBodyViewport.ts** (src/utils/tabBodyViewport.ts) — *Tab body viewport sync*: Pin TabContentsScroll height via --bonsai-tab-body-height so overflow scroll works on gamescope.
- **thinkingSummaryText.ts** (src/utils/thinkingSummaryText.ts) — *Cleaning up the "thinking" line shown while an Ask is running*: While an Ask is being answered, the screen shows a short line describing what the model is doing — "Thinking…", or something more specific once the back end sends it. This file cleans up that line if the model starts it with a throwaway filler word ("Yeah,", "Sure,", Fine.") instead of getting straight to the point, and supplies the fixed placeholder text shown for the brief moment before the back end's own line arrives.
- **troubleshootingAskHeuristic.ts** (src/utils/troubleshootingAskHeuristic.ts) — *Noticing a question that sounds like game troubleshooting*: When a question looks like it is about getting a game running well on the Deck — crashing, stuttering, a black screen, Proton issues — the plugin can offer to turn on the permission that lets it read that game's own compatibility logs, rather than turning it on automatically. This file is the plain word-matching rule that decides whether a question looks like that kind of troubleshooting question.
- **uiDocument.ts** (src/utils/uiDocument.ts) — *UI document*: Resolve the `Document` the plugin's own UI is actually rendered into.
- **uiScaleScopeBridge.ts** (src/utils/uiScaleScopeBridge.ts) — *Sharing the current text size with pop-up windows*: A pop-up window (opened with `showModal`) is drawn outside the plugin's normal on-panel area, so it cannot simply inherit the text and spacing size (the size a person picked, or the plugin worked out automatically for the screen) the same way the rest of the plugin does. This file is a small shared shelf: the main panel publishes its current size choice here, and a pop-up window reads it back so its own text and spacing match.
- **unifiedInputPersistenceMode.ts** (src/utils/unifiedInputPersistenceMode.ts) — *Deciding the one moment to clear the Ask box for "do not remember"*: The Ask box can be set to remember what was typed in it between openings, or to always start empty ("do not remember"). This file decides the one moment that starting-empty setting should actually clear whatever is currently typed: only right when the person switches into it, never on every reopening of the panel while already in that mode.
- **unwrapAskedEntitySpoilerFences.ts** (src/utils/unwrapAskedEntitySpoilerFences.ts) — *Asked-entity spoiler unwrap*: Display-time unwrap of bonsai-spoiler fences per spoiler constitution rules.
